elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The preamble defines the counterparty to our side as "Tri City National Bank, a Wisconsin corporation (including its Affiliates, \"Customer\")", so the Section 23.4 grant to "Customer" already runs to Affiliates; no new wording was added and none is needed.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered 23.4 grant runs only to "Customer"; no contractor/on-behalf-of language was inserted. Section 23.5's "(or its designee)" governs use mechanics, not the scope of the grant, and 23.5(1) still bars transfer or sublicence to third parties other than a successor.
The grant remains limited "through the end of the Term", and 23.5 speaks of use "during the term of the license granted herein"; no perpetual paid-up licence language exists.
No "irrevocable" language appears in the rendered 23.4 grant; the drafter deleted only "non-transferable".

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The rendered text contains no limitation on the grounds for ending the source-code licence; it simply expires with the Term, and no uncured-material-breach-only limitation was added.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: 23.4 now reads "a non-exclusive license, transferable to Customer's successor by merger or acquisition", and 23.5(1) is conformed with "other than Customer's successor by merger or acquisition".

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Affiliate coverage is already unconditional and broader than the fallback: "Tri City National Bank ... (including its Affiliates, \"Customer\")". The written-notice condition does not apply because no notice mechanic is required to bring Affiliates within the defined licensee.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "non-transferable" is deleted and replaced with "transferable to Customer's successor by merger or acquisition" in 23.4, and the otherwise contradictory 23.5(1) transfer/assignment bar is carved out for that same successor, so the two provisions are consistent.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: affiliate coverage is pre-existing in the defined term "Customer" (broader than the notice-conditioned fallback), and successor transferability is now express in the operative grant.

Preferred is incomplete: no contractor/on-behalf-of extension in the 23.4 grant, no perpetual or irrevocable paid-up licence (the grant is still "through the end of the Term"), and no limitation of termination to uncured material breach. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf" to 23.4, add a perpetual and irrevocable paid-up licence on payment of the licence fees, and expressly limit revocation/termination of the licence to uncured material breach.

Minimality holds: the only changes are deletion of "non-transferable" and insertion of the successor-transfer permission in 23.4, plus the narrow conforming exception in 23.5(1). The 23.5 edit is not an extra because without it the retained third-party transfer/assignment bar would contradict the new grant.

Intent preserved: the internal-use-only limitation, the Customer Data processing purpose, the service-bureau prohibition, the application/functionality scope limit, the fee condition, the escrow-release triggers and the Section 22.4 assignment mechanic all survive without contradiction or dangling references. No new Vendor assignment exception was created.

Note for the rationale (not a defect): the fallback is achieved by the redline only; the clause as drafted failed the fallback because the grant was expressly "non-transferable" and reinforced by the 23.5 bar, and Section 22.4 addresses assignment of the Agreement, not transferability of the licence.
